title_en: Dai Weijun v. Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. — dispute over recovery of labor remuneration
ruling_gist_en: Employers rewarding excellent employees and penalizing inferior employees based on a last-place elimination system, and taking measures such as job transfer and salary adjustment for low-ranked employees, is an important aspect of the enterprise's operational autonomy. As long as such job transfer and salary adjustment are based on the reasonable needs of the enterprise's production, operation, and management, and do not violate legal provisions and the rules and regulations lawfully formulated by the employer, if an employee claims that such job transfer and salary adjustment are illegal, the people's court will not support the claim.

full_text_en:
Dai Weijun v. Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. — dispute over recovery of labor remuneration

【Ruling Summary】

Where an employer adopts a rank-and-eliminate system to reward the excellent and punish the inferior among employees, and takes measures such as adjusting the position or salary of those ranked at the bottom, this constitutes an important aspect of the enterprise's operational autonomy. As long as such adjustment of position or salary is based on reasonable needs for the enterprise's production, operation, and management, and does not violate legal provisions or the rules and regulations lawfully formulated by the employer, the court does not support a worker's claim that such adjustment of position or salary is illegal.

Plaintiff: Dai Weijun, male, born on July 24, 1972, residing in Yushan Town, Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd., domiciled at Kunshan Development Zone, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Lin Bofeng, Chairman of the company.

Plaintiff Dai Weijun filed an action with the Kunshan City People's Court of Jiangsu Province against defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. regarding a dispute over recovery of labor remuneration.

Plaintiff's Allegations: During the performance of the labor contract, the plaintiff did not commit any serious disciplinary violations. However, the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd., citing a rank-and-eliminate system, transferred the plaintiff to another position, reduced his salary, and withheld his monthly and quarterly bonuses and overtime pay. Plaintiff requested the court to order the defendant to pay a wage difference of RMB 21,741.50 (including overtime pay, position salary, monthly bonuses, and quarterly bonuses) for the period from July 2015 to June 2016, and economic compensation of RMB 5,435 for the insufficient payment of wages.

Defendant's Defense: 1. The labor contract stipulates that the plaintiff Dai Weijun's position is that of an operator, and it further agrees that the company may lawfully change the plaintiff's position in accordance with work needs and the principle of good faith. 2. The company's rules and regulations clearly provide that the employee's daily records and the assessment of various monthly bonuses will serve as the basis for promotion and position transfer, of which the plaintiff was fully aware. Additionally, the plaintiff was aware of the amounts of monthly and quarterly bonuses paid but never raised any objections. The company's transfer of the plaintiff based on annual and quarterly assessment rankings and in accordance with company regulations was for operational needs. 3. The evidence provided by the plaintiff is insufficient to prove that the defendant failed to pay bonuses and overtime pay in full. In summary, the defendant requested the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

The Kunshan City People's Court of Jiangsu Province found the following facts at first instance:

Plaintiff Dai Weijun began working for the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. on November 4, 1996, as an employee in the packaging department. Starting in November 2010, Dai Weijun served as the section chief of the packaging department. The last labor contract between the parties was effective from March 1, 2014, to February 28, 2019, stipulating that Dai Weijun's position was that of an operator, that Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. could lawfully change Dai Weijun's position in accordance with work needs and the principle of good faith, that Dai Weijun's normal working hours wage was at the minimum wage standard, that the base for calculating overtime pay was the minimum wage standard, and that Dai Weijun accepted the company's adjustments and changes to his position. The "Employee Work Rules" of Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd., in the section on employee assessment, provide: "Daily records: When an employee exhibits good or bad behavior, the unit head shall notify the human resources department in writing to record it; the assessment of various monthly bonuses shall be based on the above two records as the basis for promotion and position transfer. Disciplinary actions: Demerit: fine of RMB 500-1,000; Reprimand: fine of RMB 500; Fine: fine of RMB 10-500." Dai Weijun's salary structure consisted of a base salary of RMB 4,350, a position salary of RMB 1,500, monthly bonuses (variable), quarterly bonuses (variable), bonuses (variable, generally below RMB 400 before February 2016), a food allowance of RMB 180, and holiday overtime pay.

In November 2015, the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. received a customer complaint regarding mold on glass. On December 2, 2015, Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. took disciplinary action against personnel in the packaging department, including giving Dai Weijun a reprimand and a fine of RMB 500.

On November 18, 2015, the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. issued a notice on personnel configuration review, announcing the following adjustment plan: the number of section/team chiefs was 65, and based on the annual quarterly bonus assessment rankings, the bottom 10% would be demoted. Additionally, the 2015 annual assessment summary table of Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. showed that Dai Weijun ranked 43rd out of 47 people, placing him fifth from the bottom. On January 4, 2016, Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. issued a personnel notice regarding Dai Weijun, changing his position from section chief to team leader, and reducing his position salary from RMB 1,500 to RMB 700. Starting in February 2016, Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. paid Dai Weijun a position salary of RMB 700, a bonus of RMB 950 for February 2016, and from March 2016 onward, a fixed bonus of RMB 800.

Plaintiff Dai Weijun filed an arbitration application with the Kunshan Labor and Personnel Dispute Arbitration Committee in July 2016, requesting that the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. pay a wage difference of RMB 21,741.50 for the period from July 2015 to June 2016 and economic compensation of RMB 5,435 for the insufficient payment of wages. The committee ruled to dismiss Dai Weijun's arbitration request. Dissatisfied with the arbitration award, Dai Weijun filed a lawsuit with the Kunshan City People's Court.

The Kunshan City People's Court of Jiangsu Province held at first instance:

Plaintiff Dai Weijun commenced employment with the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd., and the parties lawfully established a labor relationship. Dai Weijun's claim for a wage difference of RMB 21,741.50 for the period from July 2015 to June 2016 includes: an overtime pay differential of RMB 1,862.25 for October 2015 to February 2016; a position salary differential of RMB 4,800 for January 2016 to June 2016; a monthly bonus differential of RMB 7,944 for September 2015 to May 2016; a quarterly bonus differential of RMB 6,635 for July 2015 to May 2016; and a deduction of RMB 500 in November 2015.

Regarding the overtime pay differential of RMB 1,862.25 from October 2015 to February 2016, plaintiff Dai Weijun argued that the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. should calculate the overtime pay base using his average wage. However, the labor contract stipulated that the calculation base was the minimum wage standard, and Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. had paid Dai Weijun's overtime pay in accordance with that agreement. Therefore, Dai Weijun's claim for the differential lacked factual basis, and the court did not support it.

Regarding the position salary differential of RMB 4,800 from January 2016 to June 2016, plaintiff Dai Weijun argued that he had not committed any serious disciplinary violation, yet the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. transferred him and reduced his salary based on a rank-and-eliminate system. The court found that the parties' labor contract stipulated that Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. could lawfully change Dai Weijun's position in accordance with work needs and the principle of good faith. Whether to apply a rank-and-eliminate system to Dai Weijun's position as section chief fell within the scope of Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd.'s managerial autonomy. Dai Weijun did not accept the company's assessment summary table but provided no evidence to support his position. Furthermore, the defendant's decision to demote Dai Weijun and reduce his salary was implemented from February 2016 onward and had been in effect for several months, during which time Dai Weijun raised no objection. Additionally, Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. increased Dai Weijun's bonus portion. The court found that Dai Weijun and Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. had reached a consensus on the position adjustment, reduction in position salary, and increase in bonuses. Therefore, the court did not support Dai Weijun's claim for the position salary differential.

Regarding the monthly bonus differential of RMB 7,944 for September 2015 to May 2016 and the quarterly bonus differential of RMB 6,635 for July 2015 to May 2016, plaintiff Dai Weijun argued that the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. had withheld his monthly and quarterly bonuses. According to Dai Weijun's salary structure, his monthly and quarterly bonuses were variable, and the labor contract did not specify any provisions regarding bonuses. Therefore, it was not improper for Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. to determine the bonus amounts based on profitability, combined with Dai Weijun's daily performance and assessment results, and to pay them accordingly. Dai Weijun claimed that the company withheld his monthly and quarterly bonuses, but the quarterly assessment form he provided was only one of the bases for bonus payment. In addition to the quarterly assessment, Dai Weijun received a reprimand in December 2015, his annual assessment results were unsatisfactory, and the company also decided to demote him and reduce his salary in January 2016. All of these factors could affect Dai Weijun's monthly and quarterly bonuses. Therefore, the court found no factual or legal basis for Dai Weijun's claim for the monthly and quarterly bonus differentials and did not support it.

Regarding the deduction of RMB 500 in November 2015. In November 2015, the defendant Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. received a customer complaint regarding mold on glass. Upon verification, the situation was true, and the company imposed disciplinary sanctions and fines on personnel in the department where plaintiff Dai Weijun worked, including a reprimand and a fine of RMB 500 for Dai Weijun. Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. imposed the sanctions and fines based on the company's rules and regulations, and Dai Weijun did not dispute the event. Therefore, the court did not support Dai Weijun's claim for the return of the RMB 500 deduction.

In summary, plaintiff Dai Weijun's claim for economic compensation of RMB 5,435 for insufficient payment of wages lacked factual and legal basis. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 29 and Article 46 of the Labor Contract Law of the PRC, Article 64 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, and Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the Kunshan City People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on November 17, 2016:

Dismiss Dai Weijun's claims.

Dai Weijun, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province.

Appellant Dai Weijun argued: The adjustment of his work position by Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. violated Article 34 of the Jiangsu Province Wage Payment Regulations, as well as the contractual agreement between the parties and the relevant rules and regulations of Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. The salary reduction following the position adjustment was also illegal. He requested the court to set aside the first-instance judgment and remand the case for retrial or amend the judgment according to law.

Appellee Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. argued: The company adjusted the appellant's position based on the contractual agreement with Dai Weijun and the "Employee Work Rules" lawfully adopted. The company's actions complied with the law and the contract. The first-instance court correctly found the facts and applied the law. It requested the dismissal of the appeal in accordance with law.

The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province, upon second-instance trial, confirmed the facts found at first instance.

The Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province held at second instance:

An employer's lawful change of a worker's position and reduction of his wage level must comply with the provisions of the employer's lawfully formulated rules and regulations, but must not violate the principle of good faith by abusing its power to make unreasonable changes to the worker's position. The focus of this second-instance dispute was whether the appellee Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd.'s adjustment of the appellant Dai Weijun's position and salary based on a rank-and-eliminate system was illegal. There is no necessary connection between a worker ranking at the bottom and being incompetent for the position. Therefore, an employer's termination of a labor relationship based on a rank-and-eliminate system violates the law. However, aside from termination of the labor relationship, a rank-and-eliminate system is not per se illegal. According to the facts found in this case, Dai Weijun held the position of section chief in the packaging department of Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. before the transfer, which had a certain managerial nature and required the worker to possess more excellent and comprehensive professional skills. It is consistent with the employer's need to ensure and improve product quality to assign relatively more excellent workers to such positions based on their work performance, and it also stimulates workers' work initiative to a greater extent. Therefore, an employer's adjustment of a worker's position based on a rank-and-eliminate system should be supported under certain conditions. In this case, the labor contract between Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. and Dai Weijun expressly stipulated that Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. could lawfully change the plaintiff's position in accordance with work needs and the principle of good faith. On January 4, 2016, Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. adjusted Dai Weijun's position based on the notice on personnel configuration review and Dai Weijun's 2015 annual assessment summary table. Dai Weijun did not raise any objection after the transfer, which should be deemed as his acceptance of the transfer. In summary, this transfer did not violate the provisions of the parties' labor contract and also complied with the relevant provisions of the Labor Contract Law of the PRC; it should be deemed lawful. The resulting salary change from this transfer was also lawful. Dai Weijun's appeal arguing that the transfer was illegal and requesting Taibo Changjiang Glass Co., Ltd. to pay wage differentials and economic compensation lacked factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

Accordingly, in accordance with Item 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province rendered the following judgment on April 1, 2017:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

This judgment is final.
